title: Order Management Built Straight into SAP
summary: DataXstream's OMS Plus runs natively on SAP BTP—no integration overhead, no separate database, and AI embedded where teams already work.
body_markdown:
For a lot of SAP customers, “order management solution” means one more system to integrate, one more database to sync, and one more thing that breaks when SAP pushes an update. DataXstream built its OMS Plus platform to avoid that problem entirely, and its 20-plus-year partnership with SAP is the reason why.


## **No database, no integration, no tech debt**


Keith Fatula, vice president of Solution Engineering at DataXstream, explains the core idea simply. OMS Plus doesn’t have its own database; it’s built directly on[SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP)](https://sap.com/products/technology-platform.html) , which means it runs natively inside the SAP ecosystem instead of sitting alongside it.


“There’s no separate database,” Fatula says, “meaning there are no integrations that need to be done at all.” When a customer service rep pulls up pricing, inventory, or order history in OMS Plus, they’re seeing the same real-time SAP data everyone else in the organization sees—not a replicated or synced copy.


Get the most advanced order management system for SAP


[Learn more about DataXstream’s OMS Plus platform](https://www.sap.com/products/crm/partners/dataxstream-llc-oms-crosschannel-order-management-solution.html)


That native build also protects something SAP customers are increasingly focused on: the[clean core](https://sap.com/products/erp/rise/methodology/clean-core.html) . Because OMS Plus runs on SAP BTP rather than through custom modifications, customers can keep their core SAP intact, which Fatula describes as critical from an[Autonomous Enterprise](https://news.sap.com/tags/autonomous-enterprise/) standpoint. There’s no separate screen for employees to learn, no swivel-chair workflow between systems, and when SAP rolls out updates, OMS Plus keeps working without any catch-up integration required.


The platform is also device agnostic. Whether the user is a call center agent working a phone queue, a field account executive on a tablet, or someone at a front counter, OMS Plus runs the same way across devices without a separate build for each environment. One platform, one interface, one source of truth.


That flexibility is part of why DataXstream’s customer base spans industries. Daikin Comfort Technologies, one of the world’s largest HVAC manufacturers, selected OMS Plus to raise the bar on its customer experience—a high-volume distribution environment where order accuracy and speed directly affect relationships with contractors and dealers across North America.


## **Where AI fits in**


Fatula is clear about why DataXstream’s AI approach has resonated: the AI lives inside the screen people already use, not in a separate tool they have to switch to.


“It’s not just an additional feature,” Fatula says. “We’ve embedded it where your employees actually are, where those customer service people are working.” A rep taking an order can see a substitute suggested when an item isn’t available locally, or get a relevant prompt about the customer they’re helping, without leaving the workflow they’re already in. Because it lives in the same interface, it doesn’t disrupt how people work. It just makes each interaction a little sharper.


## **What SAP Store adds**


Being an endorsed app on[SAP Store](https://store.sap.com/) means DataXstream has already cleared SAP’s security and testing benchmarks before a customer ever evaluates the product. Fatula points to that as a real accelerator in the sales cycle—customers browsing the store already trust SAP, and that trust transfers. Deals have ranged from six to seven figures.


“They know we’re a qualified application,” Fatula says. “We’re a trusted partner.”


His advice to other partners considering SAP Store is direct: don’t just list features. “List out the benefits that your customers are already receiving from your application. Show them the connection—that your application is something they need to look into.”


For SAP customers wrestling with order management complexity, DataXstream’s pitch comes down to one idea: the fewer systems you have to stitch together, the fewer things there are to break.
